title: Pre-order and post-order
summary: The same recursion, with the visit moved before or after the children.

checkpoints.text: The first value becomes the root.
Pre-order visits a node before its children, so the root, 50, prints first.
20 prints right after 30: pre-order finishes the whole left side before it looks right.
50 30 20 40 70 60. Pre-order lists a parent before its children, so building a new tree from this order gives the same shape.
`destroy` is post-order: it visits both children before the node itself. The first node deleted is the leaf 20.
30 is deleted only after both of its children are gone. If it went first, the only pointers to 20 and 40 would be lost with it and they would leak.
The root went last. Pre-order: node, left, right. In-order: left, node, right. Post-order: left, right, node.
